subject: State Climate Legislation and Energy Permitting Reform
overview: The committee discussed Medford's electrification and composting initiatives before hosting State Senator Mike Barrett for a briefing on upcoming state climate legislation. Senator Barrett detailed proposed reforms to energy project permitting, the regulation of competitive energy suppliers, and the expansion of the state bottle bill.

items.title: Minutes and Roll Call
items.summary: The committee approved the minutes from the previous meeting.

items.title: Electrify Medford and Energy Coaching
items.summary: Brenda Pike updated the committee on the launch of the Electrify Medford outreach campaign, including the start of coach training sessions and the development of marketing materials.

items.title: Community Electricity Aggregation
items.summary: The city renewed its electricity supply contract for three years, increasing renewable energy content to 10% at a lower cost starting in 2025.

items.title: Curbside Composting and Rain Barrel Events
items.summary: Over 1,800 residents have signed up for curbside composting, and the committee planned for a rain barrel distribution event on May 8.

items.title: School HVAC Upgrades and Resilience Hubs
items.summary: Staff reported on a federal earmark request to rebuild the Willis Avenue Community Center as a resilience hub and provided an update on heat pump installations at the Andrews and McGlynn schools.

items.title: Electric Vehicle Fleet Updates
items.summary: The city is troubleshooting charging issues with a new electric street sweeper and has been awarded a grant for an electric refuse truck.

items.title: State Climate Legislation and Siting Reform
items.summary: State Senator Mike Barrett detailed a proposed omnibus climate bill intended to expedite clean energy infrastructure by streamlining local permitting through a consolidated 'comprehensive permit' process.

items.title: Energy Consumer Protections and Waste Reduction
items.summary: Senator Barrett discussed proposals to ban door-to-door sales by competitive electricity suppliers and an initiative to increase the state container deposit to ten cents.

items.title: Solar for All Grant and Communications
items.summary: The committee received brief updates on a state 'Solar for All' grant for community projects and outreach strategies from the Climate Equity Council.
